summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Heart has 4 chambers, Tricuspid (right) & Bicuspid/Mitral (left) AV valves anchored by Chordae Tendineae. SA Node (pacemaker, 70–75 bpm) -> AV Node (0.1s delay) -> Bundle of His -> Purkinje fibers. Arteries have thick Tunica Media; veins have valves.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 Valvular Architecture & Myogenic Nodal System
- **Tricuspid Valve**: 3 cusps between Right Atrium & Right Ventricle.
- **Bicuspid (Mitral) Valve**: 2 cusps between Left Atrium & Left Ventricle.
- **Chordae Tendineae**: Tough fibrous cords connecting valve cusps to **Papillary Muscles** to prevent eversion during systole.
- **SA Node ("Pacemaker")**: Generates auto-rhythmic action potentials at $70\text{--}75\text{ bpm}$.
- **AV Node ("Pacesetter")**: Imposes a **$0.1\text{-second}$ conduction delay** to permit complete atrial emptying.

### 5.2 Blood Vessel Histology
```
                          BLOOD VESSEL WALL LAYERS
                          
   TUNICA INTIMA   ──► Innermost layer; Simple Squamous Endothelium on basement membrane.
   TUNICA MEDIA    ──► Middle layer; Smooth Muscle & Elastic fibers (Much THICKER in Arteries).
   TUNICA EXTERNA  ──► Outermost layer; Fibrous Collagenous Connective Tissue.
```
